title: Advisory ordinary-test release versus enforced AGL release
question: On a fixed public synthetic corpus, does the enforced policy contain labeled release violations that an ordinary green-test policy releases, while still releasing clean controls?

treatments.label: Written rules / ordinary tests
treatments.release_rule: Release when the case's ordinary test command exits zero.
treatments.authority: Rules are advisory; the ordinary test result directly determines release.

treatments.label: Visible, nonblocking gate
treatments.release_rule: Run the same deterministic mechanism as L3 and expose the same finding, but always release.
treatments.authority: The mechanism observes but has no release authority.

treatments.label: Enforced AGL
treatments.release_rule: Release only when the fixed AGL verifier or boundary mechanism allows it.
treatments.authority: The independent verifier or boundary guard is release-authoritative.

same_candidate_rule: All four treatments must observe the same canonical candidate envelope: exact src/tests bytes plus the exact attempted action payload. A mismatch invalidates the run.
label_rule: Every corpus case must carry an independent expected_label before execution. Missing labels invalidate the run.

primary_estimand.name: violation containment
primary_estimand.numerator: Labeled violation cases blocked by the policy
primary_estimand.denominator: All corpus cases independently labeled violation

safety_estimand.name: clean-control false blocks
safety_estimand.numerator: Labeled clean controls blocked by the policy
safety_estimand.denominator: All corpus cases independently labeled clean

analysis_rules: Report integer numerators and denominators for both policies.
Do not report productivity, speed, quality, or real-world effectiveness claims.
Treat this fixed synthetic corpus as a mechanism demonstration, not a population estimate.
Do not exclude cases after execution.
If any binding drifts, any expected label is missing, any case fails to execute, or treatment candidate digests differ, emit NO_CONFIRMATORY_RESULT and omit headline metrics.
